extracted.intended_audience: PR and marketing teams producing data-driven press releases (communicators, PR agencies, in-house marketers)
extracted.subtask_description: Creating a press release announcing a proprietary data report: includes headline, lede, body structure (findings, methodology, implications, quote), multimedia assets, and distribution strategy to maximize press pickup and SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original data your competitors don't have
rubrics_metrics.description: Original data your competitors don't have
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report should be based on proprietary or exclusive data that gives journalists a reason to cover it and establishes thought leadership; listed in 'What Makes a Releasable Data Report' and repeated in the quality rubric as 'Original data'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justifies generalizations / Sample size and demographics provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample size justifies generalizations; sample size and demographics provided
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete N and demographic breakdown so findings can be generalized appropriately; part of the methodology paragraph and explicitly listed in the Quality Rubric as 'Sample size and demographics provided.' Use sample size to justify claims and note limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology defensible / Methodology disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide how the study was conducted (online, phone, observational), time period covered, margin of error, and other methodological details that make the approach defensible. Link to full methodology in boilerplate. This appears both in 'What Makes a Releasable Data Report' and in the Template's Para 2 (Methodology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprising or counter-intuitive findings / Surprising findings highlighted
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprising or counter-intuitive findings; Surprising findings highlighted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should surface at least one counter-intuitive or newsworthy finding — the hook for journalists. The headline and lede should foreground the 'most surprising or important finding' and the Quality Rubric reiterates 'Surprising findings highlighted.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Tied to broader industry trend / Implications clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Tied to broader industry trend; Implications clear
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings should be connected to a larger industry trend and the release must explain what the results mean for the industry and affected stakeholders, including suggested future trends. The Quality Rubric lists 'Implications clear' and the Template's Para 4 covers this explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format: '[Surprising Finding] in [Industry], According to New Report'
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should follow the template: "[Surprising Finding] in [Industry], According to New Report"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise, newsy headline that foregrounds the key, surprising statistic/finding and names the industry; examples provided (e.g., '67% of Remote Workers Cite Loneliness as Top Concern, New Survey Shows'). Headline should pair with a lead chart visual when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede template: concise finding + study details + implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Lede: "A new report from [Company] finds that [surprising finding]. The [study type] of [N] [respondents] reveals [implication for industry]."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start the release with a single-sentence lede that states the headline finding, the study type and sample size, and the immediate implication for the industry. This clarifies news value and credibility up front.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top Finding paragraph requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 1 (Top Finding) — Most surprising or important finding; Concrete numbers; Comparison to expectation/baseline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First body paragraph should present the top finding with precise numeric detail and contextual comparison (expectation or baseline) to make the finding meaningful and newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology paragraph requirements (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 2 (Methodology) — Sample size; Demographics surveyed; Time period covered; How conducted; Margin of error
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second paragraph must disclose methodological details: N, demographic composition, dates of data collection, mode (online/phone/observational), and margin of error. If applicable, link to a full methodology document. This supports defensibility and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Findings paragraph requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 3 (Additional Findings) — 2-3 secondary insights; Subgroup differences; Year-over-year comparisons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide 2–3 notable secondary findings, highlight any meaningful subgroup differences, and include trend comparisons (e.g., year-over-year) to add depth and story angles for different reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implications paragraph requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 4 (Implications) — What this means for the industry; What it means for affected stakeholders; Future trends suggested
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly translate findings into consequences or recommendations for the industry and stakeholders; suggest likely future trends to broaden the story beyond the headline statistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 5 (Quote) — From research lead or company executive; Substantive interpretation; Honest about limitations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short, usable quote from the research lead or an executive that adds human interpretation of the findings, acknowledges limitations, and provides a sound soundbite for journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate and access to full report
rubrics_metrics.description: Boilerplate — Standard company description; Methodology link; Full report download
rubrics_metrics.guidance: End the release with a concise company boilerplate, a link to the full methodology, and a prominent link or CTA to download the full report (the Quality Rubric lists 'Full report accessible'). These items enable deeper reporting and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia requirements (assets to include)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia Requirements — Headline chart with key finding; Infographic with multiple findings; Methodology summary visual; Customer/respondent quote graphics; Social-media-ready images
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a suite of visuals: a headline chart that illustrates the lead finding, an infographic summarizing multiple findings, a visual summary of methodology, quote graphics for social, and images optimized for social sharing. The Quality Rubric calls for 'Multimedia comprehensive'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution strategy options (how to release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution Strategy — Embargoed exclusive to top trade outlet; Coordinated release to industry press; Wire syndication for SEO; Webinar discussing findings; LinkedIn carousel breakdown; Podcast pitch on findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan a mixed release/distribution approach: consider an embargoed exclusive to a top trade outlet for top-tier coverage, simultaneous coordinated outreach to industry press, wire syndication to boost discoverability and SEO, plus owned-media follow-ups (webinar, LinkedIn carousel, podcast pitches) to extend reach and generate ongoing coverage.
